interest: This file provides unique historical evidence of how racial questions, minority interactions, and anti-Semitism were tracked in pre-World War II Japan by the U.S. State Department. It illustrates an early manifestation of modern Japanese anti-Semitism in 1933, showing how commercial resentment over foreign corporate dominance (General Electric patents) was weaponized by nationalist groups into anti-Jewish rhetoric. It also documents transnational African American cultural mobility through an entertainment tour in 1935, and highlights private American inquiries in late 1938 regarding imperial Japan's official policy toward European Jewish refugees during the escalating refugee crisis in East Asia.
keywords: Society Opposing the General Electric Patents
overview: This file (894.4016, File 242) from the Department of State's central decimal files relating to the internal affairs of Japan contains 'List of Papers' docket sheets documenting records and cross-references under the classification for race problems, racial disturbances, massacres, and pogroms in Japan between 1933 and 1938. The file contains no substantive original despatches directly attached, but instead records administrative purports and cross-references to other decimal files. Page 1 lists two cross-references: an April 19, 1933 despatch (No. 363) from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo reporting on a mass rally held by the 'Society Opposing the General Electric Patents' at which speakers attacked the Jewish race (cross-referenced to 894.543 General Electric Co./1), and a September 5, 1935 report from Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville concerning an announced tour of Japan by African American performers promoted by J.S. Fireston (cross-referenced to 331 American Negroes (Japan)). Page 2 (labeled Page #3 under the subject heading 'Recruit [Racial] matters in Japan') records a December 20, 1938 inquiry from Wallace M. Alexander requesting information on the attitude and policy of the Japanese government regarding the Jewish problem, along with a December 28 response from State Department divisions P./H and FE providing information.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a report on a mass meeting held by the 'Society Opposing the General Electric Patents' where speakers attacked the Jewish race.
keywords: Society Opposing the General Electric Patents
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports in Despatch No. 363 on an April 19, 1933 mass meeting held in Japan by an organization calling itself the 'Society Opposing the General Electric Patents'. A majority of the speakers at the gathering made the Jewish race the object of their attack. The document is cross-referenced to file 894.543 General Electric Co./1.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 363 from Grew on Anti-Semitic Meeting Opposing General Electric Patents

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to an announcement regarding a tour of Japan by African American performers promoted by J.S. Fireston.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville reports on September 5, 1935 on an announced tour of Japan by African American performers (described as American negroes). The tour was organized and promoted by J.S. Fireston. The document is cross-referenced to file 331 American Negroes (Japan).
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 145P from Neville on Tour of Japan by American Negroes

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to correspondence concerning an inquiry into the Japanese Government's attitude toward the Jewish problem and the State Department's reply.
subfiles.summary: Wallace M. Alexander sends an inquiry on December 20 requesting information regarding the attitude of the Japanese Government on the Jewish problem. On December 28, the Department of State (divisions P./H and FE) responds with information on the subject. The document is recorded under subject 'Recruit [Racial] matters in Japan' as entry No. 19.
subfiles.title: Inquiry from Wallace M. Alexander on Japanese Government Attitude Toward the Jewish Problem
